name: Switch
description: An input control that toggles between two mutually exclusive states (on and off), distinct from checkboxes in supporting only binary input with no indeterminate state.

roles.description: Identifies the element as a switch

required_attributes.description: Set to 'switch'. On <input type=checkbox role=switch> it overrides the checkbox role and the browser maps `checked` to aria-checked for you.
State. true when ON, false when OFF. Never 'mixed' — a switch is binary; that is what separates it from a checkbox.
Via aria-labelledby, aria-label, or text content

notes: Switches are for immediate effect (like toggling a setting); use checkboxes for form submissions

Use <button role='switch' aria-checked> for a setting that applies instantly. Use <input type='checkbox' role='switch'> when the value must be submitted with a form — only a real input has a form value.
A switch is binary. aria-checked='mixed' is invalid here — if you need a third state, you want a checkbox.
The visual state must not be colour alone (RAWeb 3.1): the knob's POSITION already encodes state, which is why the classic sliding design passes. A track that only changes colour does not.
Do not add aria-pressed as well — that is the toggle-button pattern. role='switch' already carries the state via aria-checked. Using both announces the state twice.
Do not change the label between 'On' and 'Off'. The label names the setting ('Email notifications'); aria-checked carries the state.
native_element: <button role="switch" aria-checked> — or <input type="checkbox" role="switch"> inside a form

raweb_criteria.reason: The on/off state must be exposed via aria-checked. A styled div with a sliding knob conveys nothing to assistive technologies.
Must toggle with Space from the keyboard, and work with any pointing device.
State must not rest on colour alone. A grey-vs-green track is invisible to a user who cannot distinguish them — add position, a label, or an icon.
The switch must show a visible focus indicator, distinct from its checked styling.
Only when built on <input type=checkbox>: as a form field it then needs a real associated label.
